title: Risk Factors, Diagnostics, and Radiological Changes of the Sacroiliac Joint After Lumbar Fusion: A Prospective Cohort Study
summary:
Background
Degenerative diseases of the spine caused by wear or deformities are common and can lead to severe back pain. When conservative treatments are insufficient, surgery may be required to stabilize the spine using screws and rods. The aim of this procedure is to reduce pain and restore spinal stability.

Despite successful surgery, many patients report persistent or newly occurring pain in the lower back or pelvic region. One possible cause of this pain is the sacroiliac joint. This joint connects the spine to the pelvis and may be exposed to increased stress or structural changes after spinal fusion. The causes and risk factors for this type of pain have not yet been sufficiently investigated.

Research Question
The aim of this study is to better understand why some patients develop sacroiliac joint pain after lumbar fusion surgery while others do not. The study will examine potential influences related to patient-specific factors, the surgical procedure itself, and changes visible in imaging studies.

Methodology
This is a prospective, non-interventional observational study. Only data that are routinely collected as part of standard medical care will be analyzed. These include information on age, sex, comorbidities, medication, muscle strength, pain levels, and quality of life, as well as imaging studies such as X-rays, CT scans, and MRI.

Data are collected before surgery and during several follow-up visits after the procedure. Participation in the study does not involve any additional examinations or risks. Medical treatment does not differ in any way from standard clinical care.
conditions: Postoperative sacroiliac joint (SIJ) pain following lumbar spinal fusion

interventions.name:
Arm 1 includes all patients scheduled for lumbar fusion surgery who meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria. This is a prospective, non-interventional observational cohort, in which only assessments that are part of routine clinical care are performed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Planned degenerative lumbar fusion surgery
• Ability to provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Contraindications to imaging
• Previous sacroiliac joint (SIJ) fusion
• Pre-existing fibromyalgia syndrome
• Ankylosing spondylitis (Morbus Bechterew)
• Known sacroiliitis
• Known bone or skeletal metastases
